title: Finite biproduct equivalence for unconditional curve assertions
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $k$ a field, $X$ a scheme and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.
Let $I$ be a finite index type and $G_a$ module sheaves on the small etale site of $X$.
Let $H$ be a module sheaf equipped with an isomorphism $e:H\simeq\bigoplus_a G_a$,
using finite biproducts [def-weil-additive-category]. The predicates $C_1,\ldots,C_8$
are those of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], with their stated conditional hypotheses.
Assume each $G_a$ and $H$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then
$(C_1(H)\land C_2(H)\land C_5(H)\land C_7(H)\land C_8(H))$ holds if and only if
$C_1(G_a)\land C_2(G_a)\land C_5(G_a)\land C_7(G_a)\land C_8(G_a)$ holds for every $a$.
There is no prime annihilator hypothesis.

source.place: Theorem 03SC, proof, fourth paragraph; Lemma 0A5C. Primary text checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SC and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A5C.

proof.text: Forgetting coefficients, inverse image, and every cohomology functor are additive, so they carry the given finite biproduct to a finite biproduct. Naturality identifies cohomology pullback and restriction with sums of the component maps. A finite sum of abelian groups is subsingleton or finite iff all its components are, and a diagonal finite sum of maps is bijective or surjective iff every component map is. Apply these facts degree by degree to C1, C2, C5, C7 and C8. The affine and proper hypotheses are common to all components. Constructibility of H follows from constructibility of all G a, closure under finite sums and transport along e; thus the conditional C5 hypotheses can be applied in both directions. Empty sums give the zero sheaf and zero cohomology, while an empty conjunction of component assertions is true. Here cohomology means the Ext-based Sheaf.H occurring in the eight predicates: Sheaf.functorH is additive, and Ext.addEquivBiproduct gives the finite product of component groups. No identification with derived global sections is used.

theorem prime_biproduct_unconditional_iff (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    {ι : Type} [Finite ι]
    (G : ι → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hGc : ∀ a, Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf (G a))
    {H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)} (e : H ≅ ⨁ G)
    (hHc : Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf H) :
    (VanishingAboveTwo Λ H ∧ VanishingAboveOneOfIsAffine Λ H ∧
      FiniteOfIsProper Λ f H ∧ BaseChangeOfIsProper Λ f H ∧
      SurjectiveRestrictionTwo Λ H) ↔
      ∀ a, VanishingAboveTwo Λ (G a) ∧ VanishingAboveOneOfIsAffine Λ (G a) ∧
        FiniteOfIsProper Λ f (G a) ∧ BaseChangeOfIsProper Λ f (G a) ∧
        SurjectiveRestrictionTwo Λ (G a)
